For developers

An API for
Glasgow’s stages.

A free, read-only JSON API for every show and venue on Glasgow Theatre. No key, no account, no tracking. 144 upcoming shows across 12 venues, refreshed with the site.

Try it in your browser ↗Download the full feed ↗

Quick start

curl -s 'https://glasgowtheatre.com/api/v1/shows?venue=tron&limit=3' | jq '.shows[] | {title, run, pricing}'

Browse this page for the contract, open the interactive examples, or point a client at OpenAPI.

Endpoints

MethodPathWhat it returns
GET/api/v1/showsFiltered, paginated shows
GET/api/v1/shows.jsonEvery upcoming show in one response
GET/api/v1/shows/{id}.jsonOne show, including every performance
GET/api/v1/shows.txtEvery show as tab-separated text
GET/api/v1/venues.jsonEvery venue, with concessions
GET/api/v1/venues/{id}.jsonOne venue
GET/api/v1/venues/{id}/showsShows at one venue; same filters as /shows
GET/api/v1/meta.jsonBuild time, refresh time and counts
GET/api/v1/openapi.jsonOpenAPI 3.1 description
GET/api/v1/schema.jsonJSON Schema for every response

Filtering

All parameters are optional. Repeat a parameter or comma-separate values to match any of them.

ParameterExampleMeaning
from, to?from=2026-10-01&to=2026-10-31Match overlapping runs, not just opening nights
date?date=2026-10-17One day; shorthand for from=to=date
venue?venue=tron,tramwayVenue ids from /venues.json
form?form=play,musicalArt form, e.g. play, dance, stand-up
tag?tag=lunchtimeAny tag, including structural ones
q?q=macbethSearch title, venue, description, producer, art form and tags
free?free=trueFree shows
payWhatYouLike?payWhatYouLike=truePay-what-you-like shows
hasPerformances?hasPerformances=trueOnly shows with a performance list
minPrice, maxPrice?maxPrice=15Filter on the published from-price
sort, order?sort=price&order=ascdate (default), closes, title, venue, price
limit, offset?limit=20&offset=20Pagination; limit is 1–200, default 50
format?format=txtTab-separated text instead of JSON

A venue

Concessions are a property of the building, not the show. They are hand-checked against the venue's own page and the date is published with them.

{
  "id": "oran-mor",
  "name": "A Play, a Pie and a Pint",
  "area": "West End",
  "description": "A lunchtime theatre programme in a converted church at the top of Byres Road. Every week brings a new short play, with a pie and a drink included in the ticket.",

What the data means

  • Dates are Europe/London calendar dates. There is no UTC offset on run.opens, run.closes or performance dates.
  • Only upcoming shows are published. The build drops expired listings, so an empty response means nothing is listed for that query.
  • Prices are a guide. pricing.from can be the cheapest seat still on sale, not the face value, especially at the King's, Theatre Royal and Pavilion. pricing.text is the venue's own wording; pricing.source says how it was read; pricing.checkedAt says when.
  • Not every show has performances. Where a venue publishes only a run, performances is empty and run.time may be the only time.
  • Accessibility is free text. It is not a structured guarantee; check the booking page.
  • Images remain the venue's copyright. Credit is included where we have it.
  • Attribution. Please credit Glasgow Theatre and link to glasgowtheatre.com when you use the data. Do not present it as official venue information.

Versioning

The path carries the version: /api/v1. Changes within v1 are additive only. A breaking change gets /api/v2 and at least twelve months of overlap.

Changelog

  • v1, October 2026. First public release: shows, venues, concessions, OpenAPI and JSON Schema.

Static snapshots and CORS

The .json endpoints are files written by the daily build; they are cached at the edge and are the safest thing to poll. The extensionless /shows endpoint is a Cloudflare Pages Function that filters the same snapshot. All endpoints send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so they can be called from a browser on any origin.

Need a language example?

Open the interactive examples for JavaScript, Python, PHP, C and Go. Each one is editable, runs in a sandbox, and is also available as a file in the repository under examples/.
